answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonding: each agent must lock real capital before it can act or vote. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, not one, so a sybil swarm grows as costly as counting grains in a dune or drops in an ocean. Misbehavior slashes the bond, so an attacker pays upfront and bleeds value, while an honest agent, rare as a flawless opal, keeps its stake and reputation intact.
